title: ADD_RELATIONSHIP keeps container state O(1) where ADD_FILE grows the drive document with every child
content:
`document-drive` keeps its child catalogue **inside the drive document's own state**, at `state.global.nodes[]`. Every `ADD_FILE` mutates that array, which means three costs grow together with child count: every replay walks every previously-added child, every read materialises the full node list, and the drive's operation log grows one entry per file. Container performance decays as the drive fills.

`ADD_RELATIONSHIP` sidesteps all three. It is a **system-scope action handled directly by the reactor's job executor** — the source document's state and operation log are untouched. The indexer writes one row to the `DocumentRelationship` table, and the graph is read back through `IDocumentIndexer`. Cost is flat in the number of children.

The `drive-override` recipe demonstrates this by building a container document whose entire schema is:

```graphql
type CustomContainerState {
  name: String!
  description: String
}
```

No `nodes`, no children, no files. It then links 10,000 children via `reactor.execute(containerId, "main", [addRelationshipAction(containerId, childId, "contains")])` and confirms `state.global` keys are still exactly `["description", "name"]`.

Enumeration is paged and DB-native rather than a state read:

- `documentIndexer.getOutgoing(containerId, ["contains"], { cursor, limit })` — children; advance `cursor` until `nextCursor` is empty.
- `documentIndexer.getIncoming(childId)` — parents. The relationship table is indexed on both `sourceId` and `targetId`, so the graph is genuinely bidirectional.

The same data is exposed over GraphQL as `documentOutgoingRelationships(documentId, relationshipTypes, paging)` and `documentIncomingRelationships(...)`, both paged, for external clients.

The trade-off: the container's reducer never sees relationships at all, so any invariant you wanted to enforce over the child set ("no more than N children", "child types must match") is no longer enforceable in the reducer. You gain flat scaling and lose reducer-level control over membership.

Provenance: academy `05-Lookup/00-Cookbook.md`, Drive Override recipe ("Why this scales better than ADD_FILE"), academy 6.2.2-dev.45.
description: document-drive mutates state.global.nodes[] per file; ADD_RELATIONSHIP is a system-scope action the job executor handles, writing one indexed row so container cost is flat in child count.
